newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli workers in Bezeq sympathy strike.
newsitem.headline: Israeli workers in Bezeq sympathy strike.

text.p: Thousands of Israeli public sector workers walked off their jobs for an hour on Wednesday to back striking employees of Bezeq Israel Telecom, shutting down Israel's main airport and Israel Radio, a union official said.

Employees of state-owned Bezeq walked out on Monday to protest the government's failure to inform them in advance of an agreement to sell 12.5 percent of Bezeq's shares to Merrill Lynch for $250 million, union officials said.
Merrill Lynch plans to sell the shares to its clients.
Bezeq filed a motion in court on Wednesday to halt the strike.

Shlomo Shani, chairman of the trade union department at the Histadrut labour federation, said workers at Israel's Airports Authority, as well as at state-owned El Al Israel Airlines and Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI), halted work for an hour in support of the Bezeq strike.
"They held an assembly in a hanger at (Tel Aviv's Ben-Gurion) airport. I just returned from there and can say that nothing moved there for an hour," Shani told Reuters.
A work stoppage at the Israeli Broadcasting Authority took Israel Radio off the air between 2 p.m. and 3 p.m. (1100 and 1200 GMT).
Shani said other public sector employees were supposed to have participated in the action but he could not confirm how wide the walk-out was.
"We are determined not to allow the government to set or change policy (over state-owned firms) without first consulting the workers," he said.

Bezeq employees, fearing privatisation of the company will lead to massive layoffs, said Communications Minister Limor Livnat had promised them that the government would not sell any shares in Bezeq without first consulting them them.
A Bezeq spokesman said the workers should not be striking since their grievance was with the government, not the company.
Shani said any further labour action will depend on the court's decision.
